key_insight: Random Forest and EEGNet led their respective model groups in Rett syndrome EEG classification, with both highlighting delta/theta activity and centro-frontal regions.
clinical_relevance: The study supports research into interpretable EEG biomarkers for Rett syndrome, not cancer drug discovery, without establishing clinical diagnostic readiness.
method: Compared PSD-based Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, and XGBoost.
Evaluated ShallowConvNet, DeepConvNet, EEGNet, and EEG Conformer on preprocessed EEG.
Explained predictions using Random Forest SHAP and EEGNet occlusion sensitivity.
evidence_signal: Resting-state, eyes-closed EEG from Rett syndrome patients and healthy controls was evaluated using subjectwise cross-validation and balanced accuracy; 4-second epochs offered the best reported performance–robustness trade-off.
watch_item: The abstract reports no sample size, numerical performance estimates, or external validation, limiting assessment of generalizability.
paper_title: EEG Biomarkers for Rett Syndrome: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning with Explainable AI
